title: Infant Sleep Machines and Hazardous Sound Pressure Levels
source_conditions: 14 infant sleep machines at maximum volume; 30/100/200 cm; correction factors for a 6-month-old's ear canal
applicability: Dedicated devices at max volume, not typical use levels; smartphones not included; the 50 dBA figure is itself borrowed from hospital nursery recommendations (1-hour average)
notes: Verified against the primary abstract 2026-11-17. All devices >50 dBA at 30 cm; 3 devices >85 dBA.

title: Continuous white noise exposure during sleep and childhood development: A scoping review
source_conditions: Scoping review: 5 databases searched from inception through June 2022; 644 publications retrieved, 20 met inclusion criteria (7 animal, 13 pediatric; 83 animal and 9428 human subjects). White noise machines can exceed 91 dB on maximum volume, exceeding NIOSH noise exposure guidelines for a 2-h work shift in adults.
applicability: Scoping review of chronic white noise exposure during sleep and childhood development; conclusion supports limitation of maximal sound intensity and duration on commercially available white noise devices. No dB cap for infant devices and no 60 dBA recommendation appear in the abstract. NIOSH limits are adult occupational guidelines used as a comparison, not an infant standard.
notes: Corrected 2026-11-18: row previously misattributed authorship, title, and content (claimed a reanalysis of 24 machines and 6 phone apps and a ~60 dBA recommendation; neither appears in the abstract). Authors: De Jong RW, Davis GS, Chelf CJ, Marinelli JP, Erbele ID (5th author), Bowe SN. Verified against the primary abstract via PubMed (PMID 38663282) 2026-11-18. Full text not retrieved. Row key retained as a stable identifier despite the corrected first authorship.

title: Preventing Excessive Noise Exposure in Infants, Children, and Adolescents (AAP policy statement, Pediatrics 2023)
source_conditions: Policy statement on noise exposure in children broadly
applicability: Reported to give distance/volume/duration guidance without a specific dB cap for infant devices
notes: Existence verified via secondary sources 2026-11-17; primary text not yet read.

title: Sound environment of the fetal sheep
source_conditions: Pregnant ewes (sheep, in vivo); hydrophone surgically implanted inside the intact amnion; SPL measured outside and inside during quiet and during sound-field exposures to broadband and octave-band noise. Stated values: +2 to +5 dB (inside minus outside) below 0.25 kHz; attenuation increasing at 6 dB per octave above 0.25 kHz; attenuation averaged 20 dB at 4.0 kHz
applicability: Animal (sheep) model, not human; nonetheless the anchor of the integrated transfer curve: the only stated transfer slope in the primary literature (6 dB/oct above 250 Hz), and the stated low-frequency range whose midpoint (+3.5 dB) sets the shelf below the 250 Hz knee
notes: PMID 2301503; Am J Obstet Gynecol 162(1):282-287. Round-2 reinforcement (2026-11-17): values quote-checked verbatim against the PubMed abstract (part of the 38/38 token check) and re-read. Underpins the integrated transfer curve (knee 250 Hz) together with richards_1992.

title: Sound levels in the human uterus
source_conditions: Human in vivo: 8 parturients (women in labor); hydrophone placed in the uterus; SPL measured for externally generated one-third-octave band noises, male and female voices, and the subject's own voice. Primary-attested values are the abstract endpoints only: enhancement averaging +3.7 dB at 0.125 kHz; maximum attenuation 10.0 dB at 4.0 kHz; mother's own voice enhanced +5.2 dB on average
applicability: Human side of the transfer evidence: used as the gentler (lower) sensitivity bound bracketing the sheep anchor, not as the anchor itself. Verification scope is the two abstract endpoints ONLY: intermediate one-third-octave band values are NOT primary-attested (full text paywalled at LWW; round-3 retrieval failed), and the 2.7 dB/oct endpoint line in the project files is derived arithmetic, not a stated value
notes: PMID 1635729; Obstet Gynecol 80(2):186-190. Round-2 (2026-11-17): abstract values quote-checked verbatim and re-read. Round-3 (2026-11-17): full text not obtained, so the scope above stands. DOI not shown on the PubMed record (per the round-2 XML), so doi/url left blank. Underpins the integrated transfer curve (knee 250 Hz) as its human lower bound. [2026-11-17 追記] PubMed (PMID 1635729) で書誌 (Obstet Gynecol. 1992 Aug;80(2):186-90) と端点 (+3.7 dB @0.125 kHz、最大減衰 10.0 dB @4.0 kHz) を再確認。DOI は PubMed 表示で確認できなかったため空欄のまま。

title: Fetal hearing
source_conditions: Human intrauterine recordings by the Querleu group (primary reports in French journals: Med Hyg 1981; J Gynecol Obstet Biol Reprod 1981; Rev Fr Gynecol Obstet 1988), known to the project only through secondary reports: hydrophone near the fetal head at the beginning of labor and after amniotomy; band attenuations of 2 dB at 250 Hz, 14 dB at 500 Hz, 20 dB at 1000 Hz, 26 dB at 2000 Hz. The registered document is the group's 1988 English review (Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol, PMID 3061844), whose abstract states only a general bound (attenuation rarely more than 30 dB)
applicability: Comparison only: the band values serve solely as the steeper human bracket in the transfer-curve comparison. Design values are NOT derived from this source, and it never moves the design anchor (round-3 rule: secondary data cannot move the anchor)
notes: Round-3 (2026-11-17): primary reports not openly accessible (French journals / paywall), so the band values could not be confirmed in a primary source; corroborated by three independent secondaries: Muenssinger et al. 2013 (Front Hum Neurosci, PMC3876038, quoted verbatim), Spence & Freeman 1996 (2 dB at 250 Hz and 20 dB at 1000 Hz attributed to Querleu et al. 1981; 2026-11-18 訂正: 旧表記 Moon & Fifer は誤帰属、正しくは spence_freeman_1996), and the Busnel et al. Fetal audition synthesis. Stored in literature/bed_transfer_curves.csv as kind=secondary_corroborated. Records discrepancy left unresolved: the round-2 XML cites the 1988 review as 28(3):191-212, the round-3 memo as 29:191-212. [2026-11-17 追記] 巻号の食い違いは解消: PubMed (PMID 3061844) の書誌は Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol. 1988 Jul;28(3):191-212 で、登録済み DOI (10.1016/0028-2243(88)90030-5) と一致する。第2弾 XML の 28(3) が正しく、第3弾メモの 29 は誤り（29 表記は一部の二次文献の参考文献リストに流通）。

title: The intrauterine sound environment of the human fetus during labor
source_conditions: Human in vivo background measurement: 10 pregnant women near term in labor; miniaturized hydrophone placed transcervically at the level of the fetal neck under ultrasonographic guidance; reported values are for the 8 women in whom no cardiovascular noise was audible. Stated: background noise predominantly below 100 Hz at 60-85 dB; above 100 Hz less than 60 dB, decreasing to 40 dB above 500 Hz (the above-100 Hz figures are stated bounds, not point values)
applicability: Describes the intrauterine background spectrum itself, NOT an external-to-uterus transfer function: it grounds the bed (blood-flow) layer's own spectral shape only and must not be cited as a transfer slope. The 8.6 dB/oct background fall in the project files is derived arithmetic from the stated bounds, not a stated value
notes: PMID 2386134; Am J Obstet Gynecol 163(2):484-490. Round-2 reinforcement (2026-11-17): abstract values quote-checked verbatim (part of the 38/38 token check) and re-read. Linked parameter is via the shared 250 Hz shaping of the bed layer; its evidentiary role is the background spectrum, not the transfer curve.

title: Newborn Infants Prefer the Maternal Low-Pass Filtered Voice, But Not the Maternal Whispered Voice
source_conditions: Article by Melanie J. Spence and Mark S. Freeman, Infant Behavior and Development 19:199-212 (1996) — a secondary source by nature, read directly by the project in round 3. Attribution statements as recorded from p.200: in Richards et al. 1992, one-third-octave bands with center frequencies below 250 Hz were enhanced up to 5 dB, and the maternal voice was measured at 77 dB in utero; Querleu et al. 1981 reported a 250 Hz tone attenuated 2 dB and a 1000 Hz tone attenuated 20 dB
applicability: Corroboration only: its role is to corroborate the attributions about richards_1992 and querleu_1988. It is NOT primary measurement data and must never anchor design values; the verification status covers Spence & Freeman's own attribution statements as read, not the underlying measurements
notes: Round-3 (2026-11-17): attribution statements read directly and recorded in literature/bed_literature_round3_human.md; the Richards below-250 Hz band detail from this source was deliberately NOT entered into the dataset. Freeman) と題名を確認し、第3弾メモが引いた2節が p.200 に逐語で存在することを確認した。混同の原因は p.199 の DeCasper & Fifer (1980) 引用と主題の近さと考えられる。旧 reference_id (moon_fifer_1996) は再利用しない。
